instruction: Please help me change the color theme of VS Code to Solarized Dark.

parameters.command: SETTINGS_PATH="$HOME/.config/Code/User/settings.json"; [ ! -f "$SETTINGS_PATH" ] && echo '{"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"}' > "$SETTINGS_PATH" || (grep -q "workbench.colorTheme" "$SETTINGS_PATH" && sed -i 's/"workbench.colorTheme": "[^"]*"/"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"/' "$SETTINGS_PATH" || jq '. + {"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"}' "$SETTINGS_PATH" > temp.json && mv temp.json "$SETTINGS_PATH")

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing VS Code color theme from 'Red' to 'Solarized Dark'. Evaluator checks if settings.json contains the correct theme value. Uses existing compare_config metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses check_json_settings metric which parses JSON and validates key-value pairs
Getter (get_vm_file) correctly fetches VS Code settings.json from /home/user/.config/Code/User/settings.json
Expected value structure is correct: when type='rule', get_rule returns config['rules'] which contains {'expected': {'workbench.colorTheme': 'Solarized Dark'}}
Metric properly handles the rules structure by accessing expected['expected'] to extract the inner dict
Verification logic correctly checks that workbench.colorTheme key has value 'Solarized Dark' regardless of JSON formatting or other settings
Complete coverage: instruction has single requirement (change theme to Solarized Dark) which is fully verified
No postconfig needed: VS Code settings.json persists after theme change via UI

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_json_settings first parameter type (str) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
metric check_json_settings second parameter type (str) may not match expected.rules type (Dict)
